text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use across every complexity tier, but documentation is too thin to tell upcoding from a genuinely complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs roughly double the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions. That uniform lift, plus the very heavy 99214 volume, is a pattern consistent with level inflation rather than a panel that is sicker in a way risk adjustment misses. Against that, the three documented 99215 claims (C0096495, C0096516, C0096694) all supported high MDM, including C0096495, a 75-year-old with no chronic conditions billed for N39.0. Only about 1% of claims have records, so the documentation can neither confirm nor rule out upcoding. The 2 of 16 moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab line are weak, not probative. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, such as C0096163, C0096213, C0096299, C0097200 and C0097892 (simple UTI, rash or abdominal pain diagnoses), and check whether the notes are templated or cloned, since supported-looking documentation on such visits would itself warrant scrutiny."}
